claims.text: Yeast, BV and trichomoniasis are the infections most often associated with vaginal symptoms
claims.quote: The infections most frequently associated with vaginal symptoms are BV (i.e., replacement of the vaginal flora by an overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria ...), trichomoniasis, and vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC).

claims.text: Yeast typically causes itching, soreness and thick curdy discharge; none of these symptoms is specific
claims.quote: Typical symptoms of VVC include pruritus, vaginal soreness, dyspareunia, external dysuria, and abnormal vaginal discharge. None of these symptoms is specific for VVC.

claims.text: Yeast signs: vulvar swelling, redness, pain, external dysuria, thick curdy discharge
claims.quote: clinically indicated by the presence of external dysuria and vulvar pruritus, pain, swelling, and redness. Signs include vulvar edema, fissures, excoriations, and thick curdy vaginal discharge.

claims.text: BV Amsel criteria: thin homogeneous milklike discharge, clue cells, pH above 4.5, fishy odor on whiff test; at least three of four
claims.quote: Homogeneous, thin discharge (milklike consistency) that smoothly coats the vaginal walls ... pH of vaginal fluid >4.5 ... A fishy odor of vaginal discharge before or after addition of 10% KOH (i.e., the whiff test)

claims.text: Amsel diagnosis requires at least three of four criteria; Nugent score from Gram stain is the reference standard laboratory method
claims.quote: Vaginal Gram stain, considered the reference standard laboratory method for diagnosing BV ... Clinical diagnosis of BV by Amsel criteria requires at least three of the following four symptoms or signs

claims.text: Yeast is associated with a normal pH below 4.5
claims.quote: vaginitis is associated with normal vaginal pH (<4.5).

claims.text: pH above 4.5 is common with BV or trichomoniasis; trichomoniasis can occur with a normal pH; pH measured with pH paper
claims.quote: The pH of the vaginal secretions can be measured by pH paper; an elevated pH (i.e., >4.5) is common with BV or trichomoniasis (although trichomoniasis can also be present with a normal vaginal pH).

claims.text: pH testing is not highly specific, so discharge should also be examined under the microscope
claims.quote: Because pH testing is not highly specific, vaginal discharge should be further examined microscopically

claims.text: In the office, pH, a KOH test and microscopy of fresh discharge can often identify the cause
claims.quote: In the clinician’s office, the cause of vaginal symptoms can often be determined by pH, a potassium hydroxide (KOH) test, and microscopic examination of a wet mount of fresh samples of vaginal discharge.

claims.text: Careful history, examination and laboratory testing to find the cause are warranted before treating
claims.quote: Therefore, a careful history, examination, and laboratory testing to determine the etiology of any vaginal symptoms are warranted.

claims.text: Yeast diagnosis: wet prep (saline or 10% KOH) showing budding yeast, hyphae or pseudohyphae, or a positive culture or other test
claims.quote: when either a wet preparation (saline, 10% KOH) of vaginal discharge demonstrates budding yeasts, hyphae, or pseudohyphae, or a culture or other test yields a positive result for a yeast species.

claims.text: Microscopy misses about half of the infections culture finds; yeast culture is the reference standard
claims.quote: the sensitivity of microscopy is approximately 50% compared with NAAT (trichomoniasis) or culture (yeast) ... Yeast culture, which can identify a broad group of pathogenic yeasts, remains the reference standard for diagnosis.

claims.text: BV NAATs can be run on clinician- or self-collected swabs in women with symptoms
claims.quote: They can be performed on either clinician- or self-collected vaginal specimens ... BV NAATs should be used among symptomatic women only

claims.text: Culture or PCR recommended in complicated yeast infection to confirm the diagnosis and identify less common species
claims.quote: Vaginal culture or PCR should be obtained from women with complicated VVC to confirm clinical diagnosis and identify non–.

claims.text: BV: normal lactic-acid-producing lactobacilli replaced by high concentrations of anaerobic bacteria
claims.quote: replacement of normal hydrogen peroxide and lactic-acid–producingspecies in the vagina with high concentrations of anaerobic bacteria

claims.text: In a nationally representative survey, most women with BV were asymptomatic
claims.quote: However, in a nationally representative survey, the majority of women with BV were asymptomatic

claims.text: BV is a highly prevalent condition and the most common cause of vaginal discharge worldwide
claims.quote: BV is a highly prevalent condition and the most common cause of vaginal discharge worldwide

claims.text: BV linked to new or multiple partners and lack of condom use
claims.quote: BV is associated with having multiple male sex partners, female partners, sexual relationships with more than one person (), a new sex partner, lack of condom use

claims.text: Whether BV results from a single sexually transmitted pathogen is unknown; routine partner treatment not recommended
claims.quote: whether BV results from acquisition of a single sexually transmitted pathogen is unknown ... Therefore, routine treatment of sex partners is not recommended.

claims.text: BV raises risk of acquiring STIs and of pregnancy complications including preterm birth
claims.quote: Women with BV are at increased risk for STI acquisition ... symptomatic BV has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including premature rupture of membranes, preterm birth

claims.text: Yeast infection is usually not sexually transmitted
claims.quote: Although VVC is usually not sexually transmitted, it is included in this section

claims.text: Estimated 75 percent of women will have at least one yeast infection
claims.quote: An estimated 75% of women will have at least one episode of VVC

claims.text: Trichomoniasis: yellow-green or malodorous discharge with or without irritation; sexually transmitted; most have minimal or no symptoms
claims.quote: women with trichomoniasis sometimes have vaginal discharge, which can be diffuse, malodorous, or yellow-green with or without vulvar irritation ... The majority of persons who have trichomoniasis (70%–85%) either have minimal or no genital symptoms

claims.text: Odor is not among the typical yeast symptoms; amine odor on KOH suggests BV or trichomoniasis
claims.quote: samples that emit an amine odor immediately upon application of KOH suggest BV or trichomoniasis

claims.text: Yeast regimens: single 150 mg oral fluconazole or topical clotrimazole, miconazole, tioconazole (OTC), butoconazole, terconazole (Rx); courses single dose to 7 days, some 7 to 14 days
claims.quote: Clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7–14 days ... Miconazole 2% cream ... Tioconazole 6.5% ointment ... Butoconazole 2% cream ... Terconazole 0.4% cream ... Fluconazole 150 mg orally in a single dose

claims.text: Pregnancy: only 7-day topical azoles; single 150 mg fluconazole might be associated with miscarriage and birth defects and should not be used
claims.quote: Only topical azole therapies, applied for 7 days, are recommended for use among pregnant women. Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used.

claims.text: BV recommended regimens: oral metronidazole, metronidazole gel, clindamycin cream (5 or 7 days)
claims.quote: Metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days ... Metronidazole gel 0.75% ... once a day for 5 days ... Clindamycin cream 2% ... at bedtime for 7 days ...

claims.text: BV alternatives: oral clindamycin, clindamycin ovules, secnidazole single dose, tinidazole 2 or 5 days (single dose to 7 days)
claims.quote: Clindamycin 300 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days ... Clindamycin ovules 100 mg* ... Secnidazole 2 g oral granules in a single dose ... Tinidazole 1 g orally once daily for 5 days

claims.text: BV in pregnancy: treat all symptomatic pregnant women; any recommended regimen can be used
claims.quote: BV treatment is recommended for all symptomatic pregnant women ... Pregnant women can be treated with any of the recommended regimens for nonpregnant women

claims.text: Tinidazole and secnidazole should be avoided in pregnancy
claims.quote: Thus, tinidazole should be avoided during pregnancy (). Data are insufficient regarding efficacy and adverse effects of secnidazole ... during pregnancy; thus, their use should be avoided.

claims.text: Using the wrong over-the-counter product can delay treatment of the real cause
claims.quote: Unnecessary or unapproved use of over-the-counter preparations is common and can lead to a delay in treatment of other vulvovaginitis etiologies, which can result in adverse outcomes.

claims.text: Symptoms persisting after an OTC product or returning within 2 months should be evaluated and tested
claims.quote: any woman whose symptoms persist after using an over-the-counter preparation or who has a recurrence of symptoms <2 months after treatment for VVC should be evaluated clinically and tested.

claims.text: Recurrent yeast can be idiopathic or linked to antibiotics, diabetes or host factors; most have no apparent underlying condition
claims.quote: Recurrent VVC can be either idiopathic or secondary (related to frequent antibiotic use, diabetes, or other underlying host factors). ... the majority of women with recurrent VVC have no apparent predisposing or underlying conditions.

claims.text: Persistent or recurrent BV is common and a reason to return for evaluation
claims.quote: Because persistent or recurrent BV is common, women should be advised to return for evaluation if symptoms recur.

claims.text: PID is often missed when signs such as abnormal bleeding or discharge are mild or nonspecific
claims.quote: others are not diagnosed because the patient or the health care provider do not recognize the implications of mild or nonspecific symptoms or signs (e.g., abnormal bleeding, dyspareunia, and vaginal discharge).
